anna-m: Heads up — saw a p99 / tokens/sec regression after yesterday's kernel-picker tweak on Mixtral-7B. Rooted to a single deploy window. Posting quick numbers and profile output.

miguel: Can you paste the p50/p99 + tokens/sec? And which cluster?

anna-m: us-west-gpu-prod. Before: p50 65ms, p99 210ms, 11.2k tok/s. After: p50 86ms, p99 340ms, 6.8k tok/s.

perf-bot: profile job #452 finished — /artifacts/452/mixtral7b/kern_profile.json

anna-m: Here's the short profile snippet:
```
kernel_selector: selected "matmul_fused_v2" fallback_count=37
batching: avg_batch_size 3.1 -> 1.9 (spike in small batches)
kv_cache: hit_rate 0.78 -> 0.62
tokenizer: avg_tokens_per_prompt 118 -> 156 (byte-fallback events + extra BOS tokens)
```

sophie: Interesting — tokenizer jump stands out. We recently enabled byte-fallback for a small set of inputs; if token counts increase, batching heuristics drop avg batch size and kernel selection may flip to slower matmul path.

ryan: Also seeing more KV misses => cold starts for cache shards. Did the picker change alter max_seq heuristic?

anna-m: We changed the `kernel_picker.seq_threshold` from 1024 -> 512 to force fused kernels earlier for longer contexts. Might be causing more kernel mismatches when tokenized length spikes.

miguel: That threshold change could make the runtime pick a kernel expecting different RoPE scaling behavior. Any RoPE mismatches between the quantized Mixtral build and the runtime kernels?

anna-m: Quick check: model meta says rope_scale=1.0, runtime fallback kernel assumed scale 0.5 in the new selector branch (oops).

sophie: That explains extra work per attention op and also why kv cache layout differed (heads/kv dims path changed). Kernel picks with wrong RoPE scaling can force a fallback codepath that is less optimized.

ryan: Tossing a small table from perf traces:
```
run    | kernel         | p50 | p99 | tok/s | kv_hit
before | matmul_fused_v1 | 65ms|210ms|11.2k | 0.78
after  | matmul_fused_v2 | 86ms|340ms|6.8k  | 0.62
```

anna-m: Repro steps I'm running locally:
1) checkout kernel-picker revert branch
2) profile with `./bin/profile --model mixtral-7b --prompts chatset-50`
3) compare tokenizer logging (`--dump-tokenization`)

miguel: Can you dump tokenization for one of the failing prompts? I want to see where byte-fallback triggers and if BOS/EOS doubled.

anna-m: Pasting one example token counts: system(12) + user(96) + assistant_history(48) = 156 tokens. Previously same inputs yielded 110 tokens. Diff due to: byte-fallback on emoji, and we accidentally inserted an extra BOS token in chat template when doing canonicalization.

sophie: Oof the extra BOS was from the new chatfmt normalization change. That plus byte-fallback pushes many requests over the kernel-picker boundary, breaking batching heuristics.

infra-bot: deploy:kernel-picker/selector v2 rolled at 2026-03-17T18:40Z by @deploy-bot (canary 3/10)

anna-m: Plan: revert selector threshold + patch chatfmt to avoid duplicate BOS. Will run a canary with profiling and KV hit tracking.

miguel: Add a unit/regression test that asserts token counts for canonical chat prompts (no surprises). And add a perf-check to CI to detect >15% tok/s regressions on sample workloads.

ryan: I'll wire KV-cache metrics alerts to include shard cold-start counts so we catch this earlier.

anna-m: Opening ticket RW-1258 with logs and perf artifacts and will push revert PR now. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

sophie: thanks — please ping #eng-oncall if canary looks bad.

perf-bot: opened RW-1258 (perf/regression) — including artifact bundle /artifacts/452/

anna-m: moving to rollback and smoke test, will update thread when canary completes.
